content_metadata.learning_objective: To understand the history and evolution of English spelling and silent letters.

script.discovery:
Centuries ago, English speakers actually pronounced both letters out loud. You would literally say kuh-night and kuh-nee.
Over time, that combination felt awkward to say quickly, so speakers slowly dropped the hard K sound.
Then the printing press arrived in England. Early printers locked the spelling in place just as the spoken sound was disappearing.
So knight kept its old spelling, while the way people actually spoke moved on.
script.hook: Have you fought with English words keeping letters you do not pronounce?
script.payoff:
That means silent letters are not just random mistakes. They are linguistic fossils trapped in time.
What silent letter drives you completely crazy?
